name: Example: Finding the Parametric Equation of the Plane Passing Through Three Given Points
problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(-1,4,-3),$ $B(7,5,4),$ and $C(2,-2,8).$
worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). Let's use the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨7,5,4⟩-⟨-1,4,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨8,1,7⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =⟨2,-2,8⟩-⟨-1,4,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-6,11⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $\mathbf{a}=\langle -1,4,-3 \rangle$ of the point $A,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =a+s\overset{\to }{AB}+t\overset{\to }{AC} \\ r & =⟨-1,4,-3⟩+s⟨8,1,7⟩+t⟨3,-6,11⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

**Watch out!** The form of the final equation depends on our choice of vectors and the point on the plane. We could have picked other vectors. Likewise, we could have chosen $B$ or $C$ instead of $A$ as our point on the plane. So, the answer is *not unique*!
